explanation: With provideClientHydration(), Angular adopts the existing DOM and attaches listeners, avoiding a flash and extra work.

prompt: Where should code that reads localStorage go in an SSR app?

options.text: In afterNextRender(), which runs only in the browser
In the constructor, before anything else

explanation: Constructors, field initializers, and ngOnInit also run on the server, where localStorage does not exist.

prompt: How does Angular avoid calling the same API on the server and again in the browser?

options.text: It does not; every request runs twice
The HTTP transfer cache embeds GET/HEAD responses in the HTML for HttpClient to reuse
The browser blocks the second request

explanation: provideClientHydration() enables the transfer cache. Requests with an Authorization header are not cached by default.

prompt: With incremental hydration enabled, what does @defer (hydrate on viewport) { <app-reviews /> } do?

options.text: Skips server rendering of the reviews entirely
Renders the reviews on the server and loads/hydrates their JavaScript when they scroll into view
Prerenders the reviews at build time

explanation: The HTML is shown immediately; hydration (downloading and running the code) waits for the trigger.

prompt: Which of these breaks hydration?
explanation: Changing the DOM behind Angular's back makes the browser DOM differ from the server's, which causes hydration mismatch errors.

prompt: Which attribute should you add to the single largest above-the-fold image when using NgOptimizedImage?
explanation: priority loads the key image eagerly with high fetch priority. Other images are lazy-loaded by default.

prompt: When can you deploy only the dist/my-app/browser folder to a static host?

options.text: When every route is prerendered or client-rendered
When at least one route uses RenderMode.Server

explanation: Any route using RenderMode.Server needs the Node.js server in the server folder to run for each request.

prompt: In a zoneless app, a setInterval callback does this.count++ on a plain field. What happens to the view?

options.text: It does not update, because nothing notifies Angular; use a signal
It updates because the interval is patched
It updates on the next click only if OnPush is off

explanation: Without Zone.js, Angular only checks after a notification such as a signal write, an event binding, an async pipe emission or markForCheck().

prompt: Why is detectChanges() called from ngAfterViewInit risky?

options.text: It runs synchronously and can cause ExpressionChangedAfterItHasBeenCheckedError

explanation: detectChanges() checks immediately. markForCheck() just schedules a check for the next pass, which is safer.

prompt: What does TestBed provide for a component test?

options.text: A fresh, isolated Angular injector and compiled component tree per test, without booting the whole app

explanation: TestBed builds a throwaway module and injector so each test starts clean and components render in isolation.

prompt: Why prefer await fixture.whenStable() over fixture.detectChanges() in zoneless tests?

options.text: It waits for Angular's reactive scheduling to settle, matching production, while detectChanges() forces a synchronous pass that can mask scheduling issues

explanation: whenStable() waits for Angular's own scheduling to settle, the way production does; detectChanges() forces a synchronous pass that can hide scheduling problems.

prompt: What problem do Angular CDK Component Harnesses solve?

options.text: They make tests run in a real browser
They replace brittle CSS-selector/DOM queries with a stable, behavior-based API, so markup refactors don't break tests

explanation: A harness exposes methods like click()/getText(); only the harness's internal selectors change when markup does.

prompt: Why do locatorFor()/locatorForAll() return functions rather than cached element references?

options.text: So they re-query the DOM on each call, staying correct across @if/@for re-renders
Because Angular requires all locators to be async

explanation: Control-flow blocks destroy and recreate nodes, so a cached reference would go stale; re-querying keeps it valid.

prompt: In a Vitest project (the default since Angular 21), which API wraps an existing service method so you can assert on its calls?
explanation: vi.spyOn wraps the real method so you can assert calls and optionally replace the implementation. Jasmine and Jest spy APIs do not exist in a Vitest project.

prompt: Which adapter creates a HarnessLoader from a TestBed ComponentFixture (e.g. ____.loader(fixture))?
explanation: TestbedHarnessEnvironment.loader(fixture) bridges a TestBed fixture to the CDK harness system.

prompt: What is the fundamental difference between a Cypress E2E test and a TestBed unit test?

options.text: Cypress boots the actual compiled app in a real browser with real clicks, routing, and network calls; TestBed runs components in a simulated, isolated environment
TestBed uses a real browser; Cypress simulates the DOM

explanation: Cypress proves a user can complete a flow end to end; TestBed proves a unit behaves correctly in isolation.

prompt: What does Cypress's 'retry-ability' mean?

options.text: Failed tests are automatically re-run three times
Commands and assertions are automatically retried against the live DOM until they pass or a timeout elapses
Cypress retries the whole spec on network errors
You must manually retry each command

explanation: Auto-retrying until an element is actionable removes the need for arbitrary manual waits and reduces flakiness.

prompt: How do you make an E2E test independent of a live backend for a specific request?

options.text: Use cy.intercept() to observe or stub the request (optionally with a fixture), alias it, and cy.wait('@alias')
Disable the network in the browser

explanation: cy.intercept stubs the response so the test is deterministic and doesn't depend on real backend data.

prompt: Why should you use data-cy attributes instead of CSS classes or IDs for selectors?

options.text: They exist solely for testing and are decoupled from styling/behavior, so redesigns don't silently break tests

explanation: Dedicated test hooks survive markup and styling refactors that would break class/ID-based selectors.

prompt: Why is cy.wait(3000) considered a bad practice for waiting on a response?

options.text: It is not a valid command
It's slow when the response is fast and still flaky when it's slow; cy.wait('@alias') waits exactly as long as needed
It only works in headless mode

explanation: Aliasing an intercept and waiting on it waits precisely for the request, unlike a hardcoded arbitrary delay.

prompt: Which Cypress API caches authenticated browser state across tests so you don't re-login for every test?
explanation: cy.session() caches cookies/localStorage per session key, keeping large suites fast while assertions stay independent.

prompt: A rule that formats a price string is easiest and cheapest to cover with which kind of test?

options.text: A unit test of the function
A component test through a harness of the whole page

explanation: Test at the lowest level that can catch the bug. Pure logic belongs in fast unit tests.

prompt: A zoneless test calls fixture.detectChanges() after every action and always passes, but the real app sometimes fails to update. What is the likely problem?

options.text: The test supplies the change detection that the app lacks, hiding a missing notification
detectChanges() is not allowed in tests

explanation: Forced synchronous checks can mask state that never notifies Angular. await fixture.whenStable() matches production scheduling.

prompt: What does a static with(filters) method returning a HarnessPredicate let test authors do?

options.text: Select one specific instance, for example loader.getHarness(ToggleHarness.with({ label: 'Email' }))

explanation: HarnessPredicate narrows which matching host elements a loader returns, using options you define.

prompt: What does http.get<Order>('/api/orders/1') guarantee at runtime?

options.text: That the response body matches the Order interface
Nothing about the shape: the generic only tells the compiler what you expect
That the response is an instance of the Order class
That missing fields are filled with defaults

explanation: Types are erased at runtime. The generic is a promise to the compiler, not a check. Validate data at the boundary if you need guarantees.

prompt: Match each kind of code to the TypeScript construct it should usually use.
explanation: Interfaces describe plain data, type aliases express unions and derived types, and classes hold behavior that Angular instantiates and injects.

prompt: Which type accepts any value but forces you to narrow it before you can use it?
explanation: unknown is the safe replacement for any at trust boundaries such as JSON.parse results, caught errors, and postMessage data.

prompt: Which of these narrow a value to a more specific type? (Select all that apply)
explanation: typeof, instanceof, and in are real runtime checks that TypeScript understands. A cast with 'as' checks nothing; it only silences the compiler.

prompt: Why add a default branch that calls assertNever(question) in a switch over a discriminated union?

options.text: It makes the switch run faster
It logs unknown values in production
The compiler errors as soon as a new union member is added but not handled
It converts the union into an enum

explanation: If every case is handled, the value is 'never' in the default branch. A new, unhandled member makes it not-never, so passing it to assertNever fails to compile.

prompt: Given interface ExerciseSet { id: string; exercise: string; reps: number }, which type best describes an entry that hasn't been saved yet (the server assigns the id)?
explanation: Omit removes the id but keeps every other field required. Partial would make every field optional, which is too loose for a create payload.

prompt: Match each item to the folder it belongs in.

pairs.left: A presentational Badge component and a duration pipe
DiaryStore and the diary edit page

explanation: core/ holds app-wide singletons and the shell, shared/ holds feature-agnostic building blocks, and each feature folder holds its own pages and state.

prompt: The diary feature needs an exercise picker that currently lives in features/exercises. What should you do?

options.text: Copy the file into the diary folder and keep both in sync
Move the picker to shared/ if it's generic, so both features import it from there
Merge the two features into one folder

explanation: Features shouldn't import from each other. A generic, reusable piece belongs in shared/; an app-wide service belongs in core/.

prompt: app.routes.ts uses loadComponent for the diary page, but the page still appears in the main bundle. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: Lazy loading only works in development builds
The page is also imported statically somewhere that the main bundle includes, such as the top of app.routes.ts
The page component is missing standalone: true

explanation: A single static import pulls the code back into the main bundle. Keep feature code behind dynamic import() calls only. (Standalone is the default since Angular 19.)

prompt: Which route property registers a service shared by a route and all of its child routes?
explanation: Route-level providers create an injector for that route subtree, so every page in the feature gets the same instance without using the root injector.

prompt: Which tools help keep bundles small as the app grows? (Select all that apply)

options.text: withPreloading(PreloadAllModules) for background loading of lazy chunks
@defer for heavy, non-critical parts of a page
A SHARED_IMPORTS array spread into every component

explanation: Budgets catch growth, preloading and @defer keep the first load small. A giant shared imports array does the opposite: every component depends on everything.

prompt: What is the standalone-era version of the 'single-module app' anti-pattern?

options.text: One shared imports list (or one flat folder) that every component depends on

explanation: Both anti-patterns remove boundaries: everything depends on everything, so nothing can be found, split, or owned separately.

prompt: What does @defer (on viewport; prefetch on idle) { <app-chart /> } @placeholder { … } do?

options.text: Renders the chart immediately and hides it until scrolled into view
Downloads the chart's code when the browser is idle, and renders it when the placeholder scrolls into view
Loads the chart on the server only

explanation: prefetch on idle fetches the code early without rendering it; on viewport renders it once the placeholder becomes visible.

prompt: What is the strongest reason to split an Angular app into micro frontends?

options.text: It always makes the app load faster
Several teams need to build and deploy their parts independently
It removes the need for a design system
Angular apps can't be lazy-loaded otherwise

explanation: Micro frontends are mainly an organizational pattern. They usually cost performance and consistency, so they pay off when teams truly need independent deploys.

prompt: Which split follows the 'slice vertically' rule?

options.text: A header micro frontend, a forms micro frontend, and a services micro frontend
One micro frontend per CSS framework
An exercise-catalog micro frontend and a checkout micro frontend, each with its own UI, state, and API calls

explanation: Vertical slices cover a whole business capability, so each team can ship features alone. Horizontal slices need several teams for every change.

prompt: Match each part of an Angular component to what Angular Elements turns it into.

pairs.right: A maxItems property and a max-items attribute
A 'saved' CustomEvent with the value in event.detail
A custom element registered with customElements.define()

explanation: Inputs become properties (and dash-case attributes), outputs become DOM CustomEvents, and the component is registered as a custom element.

prompt: An Angular host must load an Angular Element built with the CLI's application builder. Which are needed? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Build the element zoneless so the page doesn't get two copies of zone.js
Add CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA to the host component that uses the tag
Declare the element's component in the host's NgModule

explanation: Only one zone.js can run per page, the builder outputs ES modules, and the host compiler must accept the unknown tag. The host never imports the element's component.

prompt: Which function from @angular/elements wraps a component so it can be registered as a custom element?
explanation: createCustomElement(Component, { injector }) returns a class you pass to customElements.define().

prompt: Why should each micro frontend release be deployed to a versioned URL like /mfe/exercise-form/1.4.0/main.js?

options.text: Browsers refuse to load unversioned scripts
So the host can pin, upgrade, and roll back deliberately instead of being broken by another team's deploy or by stale caches

explanation: With outputHashing set to none, versioned paths are what keep caching and independent deploys safe.

prompt: Which declaration needs an explicit type annotation?

options.text: const items = signal<Product[]>([]) because an empty array would infer never[]
A callback parameter in items.map((item) => item.id)

explanation: An empty array or null initial value gives no information, so annotate it. Obvious initial values and callback parameters are inferred.

prompt: Feature A needs a UI component that currently lives in feature B. What is the recommended fix?

options.text: Move the component down into shared, used by both
Import it directly from feature B
Make feature B import feature A as well

explanation: Features must not depend on each other. Code needed by two features moves down a layer.

prompt: A custom element needs to receive an array of objects from the host page. What is the right way?

options.text: Set it as a DOM property from JavaScript, since attributes can only carry strings
Put JSON in an attribute without parsing

explanation: Attributes are strings. Complex data is passed through properties on the element instance.
